## Master's Thesis

### Roads, Market Access and Forest Loss: Evidence from Ghana
*Sciences Po, Paris — Supervisor: [Prof. Clément Imbert](https://sites.google.com/site/clemimbert/)*

This thesis studies whether road-induced improvements in market access affect forest loss in Ghana. Using digitized road upgrades, district-level forest-loss data, and a spatial trade model, I find that a 1% increase in market access lowers expected annual forest loss by about 0.38%. The evidence suggests that better connectivity shifts agricultural adjustment toward input intensification rather than land expansion.

**Methods:** structural trade modelling · panel IV · Google Earth Engine · high-resolution land-cover data.

[BAKPA_thesis.pdf](https://github.com/abdulbaaribakpa/Master-thesis/blob/main/BAKPA_thesis.pdf) · [Code](https://github.com/abdulbaaribakpa/Master-thesis.git)
